# onpager_service (Resource)

Manage an OnPager service, its owner team and active state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "onpager_service" "example" {
  name    = "API"
  team_id = var.team_id
}

variable "team_id" {
  description = "Existing active owning team UUID."
  type        = string
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Nonempty name without leading or trailing whitespace. Unique case-insensitively within the tenant, including inactive records.
- `team_id` (String) Owning team UUID. Changes transfer the existing service without replacing its UUID. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID.

### Optional

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the object is active. Defaults to `true`. Changes disable or reactivate the existing UUID. Disabled objects remain in state; refresh and import never reactivate them.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Stable nonzero canonical lowercase OnPager UUID.

## Import

Import using the service UUID. Import reads the current owner and settings. A
later apply reconciles `active`; set `active = false` to keep the service
inactive.

Use an `import` block:

```terraform
import {
  to = onpager_service.example
  id = "22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222"
}
```

Or use the CLI:

```shell
terraform import onpager_service.example 22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222
```

## Lifecycle

Changing `team_id` transfers the existing service UUID. When ownership and other
settings change together, the transfer runs first and its committed result is
saved before later writes. The destination team must be active. Configured
channels that are unavailable to the destination can block transfer; resolve
that precondition explicitly.

Destroy disables the service and its active alert-filter revisions, preserving
history. Externally disabled services remain managed. Reactivation requires an
active owner and does not reactivate filters. The inactive service's name
remains reserved; import its existing UUID to manage it again.

Rename, transfer and active-state commands use the unversioned API without
revision preconditions. Failures retain state. A successful transfer is retained
if a later operation fails.

## Permissions

Requires `services.read`, `services.create`, `services.update`,
`services.disable` and `services.reactivate` in the owning team for the
corresponding operations. Transfer requires `services.update` in the previous
team and `services.create` in the destination team.
